written: 2026-09-28, after the pre-registered LG M50 comparison ended NOT MET (voltage RMSE about 150 mV, capacity +3 %) and after a labelled post-hoc diagnostic; before any run of this follow-up
why_this_follow_up: The post-hoc diagnostic located the error in (a) a model capacity about 3 % above the cells' and (b) an equilibrium voltage offset of about 45-50 mV at C/10 that remains on a capacity-normalised axis. Both are what a wrong electrode balance produces. This follow-up asks whether ONE identifiable correction of that balance, calibrated on a near-equilibrium curve only, predicts the held-out curves within the ORIGINAL criteria.
does_not_change: the pre-registered outcome of big14-a-lgm50-validation stays NOT MET; this is a new, separately registered question
data: the same pinned files as big14-a-lgm50-validation (benchmarks/measurements/chen2020_lgm50/manifest.json)

model.primary: PyBaMM SPM, Chen2020, lumped thermal, the heat-transfer coefficient calibrated in big14-a-lgm50-validation (3.555 W/m2K)
calibrated_parameters: Negative electrode active material volume fraction (Chen2020: 0.75), as a multiplicative factor in [0.85, 1.10]
Positive electrode active material volume fraction (Chen2020: 0.665), as a multiplicative factor in [0.85, 1.10]

calibration.curve: cell02 at C/10 only (0.5 A, near equilibrium)
calibration.objective: voltage RMSE over the measured samples to the earlier of the two 2.5 V ends, plus the delivered-capacity mismatch in the same units (1 % capacity counted as 10 mV), least squares

held_out: every other curve: cell02 at C/2, 1C, 1.5C; cell03 and cell04 at all four rates

acceptance_primary.scope: SPM with the calibrated balance, C/2, each of the three cells (the same V1 and C1 as big14-a-lgm50-validation)
acceptance_primary.met_if: V1 and C1 on all three cells

reported_not_judged: all rates and cells for SPM and DFN with the calibrated balance
the calibrated factors, their calibration residual, and the C/10 held-out cells as a check of the calibration itself
stated_limits: two parameters from one near-equilibrium curve: the correction is identified, not measured independently
a met outcome would show the balance correction transfers across rates; it would not validate the SPM model form, whose rate-dependent error is measured separately
independence of the data from the Chen2020 parameterisation stays UNCONFIRMED
no_change_after_seeing_results: calibration curve, parameters, bounds, held-out set and criteria are fixed
